# `jd2time()` {#fn-jd2time}

**Validation on 2.0.9005.** Build 2.0.9005 passed all 499 calendar, clock, era, angle and setting checks in A01. The largest discrepancy across 240 absolute Julian dates was 0.000021 seconds. [A01 results](a01-calendar-checks.qmd).

[Function index](function-index.html#idx-jd2time)

```{=html}
<p>An instant is specified by its UT Julian date. To label it consistently, choose the
calendar and the offset or civil timezone appropriate to the record. The conversion
rounds to the nearest second, applies the offset at the rounded instant, handles day
rollover and converts the day number with Swiss Ephemeris.
</p>
<p>Fixed offsets may be numeric hours east of UTC (for example 5.5), or
strings such as <code>"UTC+05:30"</code>, <code>"UTC-02"</code> or <code>"GMT+01"</code>.
Offsets must lie between -14 and +14 hours. UTC, GMT and the empty string
mean zero offset; an empty string does not select the system timezone.
</p>
```

**Interpretation and limits.** For an ancient event near local midnight, retain the UT Julian day alongside the printed date. Round-tripping a civil label tests conversion conventions; it cannot establish the prehistoric difference between terrestrial and rotational time.

See Details.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>calendar</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Output calendar: G or Gregorian, J or Julian. Defaults to the package calendar setting, initially Gregorian.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>verbose</code></th><td><code>F</code></td><td><p>Logical; display a conversion message. Default is FALSE.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><h5>Return value</h5><p>A character vector in YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM:SS format. Years are signed as needed and are not padded to four digits.
```{=html}
</p>
```

**Implementation.** `R/dates.R`.
